[BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690v2) explicitly identifies the discrepancy: interior-mask reconstruction uses left and right context; next-item inference appends a reserved mask after the observed prefix. Its original training also includes final-item masking. This motivates paired diagnostics, but does not establish that reconstruction margins predict validation HR@10.

Proposed probe, rather than a published established protocol: select identical public training targets and fixed candidate sets; compare interior reconstruction, the same positions with all attention paths from suffix tokens blocked at every layer, and prefix-only appended-mask prediction. Keep position IDs, prefix tokens and corruption fixed in the attention ablation; separately vary padding/position placement to quantify positional effects. Report paired loss, target rank and margin differences, stratified by prefix length and target position. Check that changing an inaccessible suffix leaves prefix-only scores unchanged, the supervised target occurrence is replaced by the reserved mask, padding cannot contribute attention, and left-padded readout selects the actual final nonpadding position—including the appended mask—rather than count−1.

For one shared BERT4Rec model, measure reconstruction-versus-endpoint gradient cosine, norms and dot products separately for item embeddings, positional embeddings, attention and feed-forward layers. [GradSplit (2023)](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/WACV2023/papers/Deng_Split_To_Learn_Gradient_Split_for_Multi-Task_Human_Image_Analysis_WACV_2023_paper.pdf) provides layerwise conflict-frequency precedent; [SAM-GS (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06130) emphasizes magnitude imbalance alongside direction. Interpret these as local optimization diagnostics: [ForkMerge’s analysis (2023)](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/60f9118a849e8e9a0c67e2a36ad80ebf-Paper-Conference.pdf) shows gradient conflict need not imply negative transfer. Its branch-merging algorithm is outside this experiment’s constraints. Only fixed macro validation HR@10 establishes recommendation improvement.
